gloss: this side up; do not turn over

definitions.gloss: this side up; do not turn upside down
definitions.explanation: A label on boxes and parcels warning that they must not be turned upside down. Literally "top and bottom: no (turning) allowed"; it does not mean that top and bottom don't matter.

examples.japanese: ⟦{箱|はこ}→箱：02162_hako⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「{天地無用|てんちむよう}」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}いてある→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
{天地無用|てんちむよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦シール→シール：09597_shiiru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{貼|は}って→貼る：10447_haru⟧⟦{送|おく}った→送る：00742_okuru⟧。
examples.english: I put a "This side up" sticker on it and sent it.

examples.japanese: {天地無用|てんちむよう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧「⟦{上下|じょうげ}→上下：04282_jouge⟧⟦どちら→どちら：00927_dochira⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧」⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}っている→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Some people think "tenchi muyō" means "either way up is fine."

notes:
{天地|てんち} (top and bottom; literally heaven and earth) + ⟦{無用|むよう}→無用：31478_muyou⟧ (forbidden, as in {立入無用|たちいりむよう}).

WATCH OUT:
Because ⟦{無用|むよう}→無用：31478_muyou⟧ usually means "unnecessary," many Japanese speakers read the label as "no need to worry which way up," the opposite of its meaning. Shippers often add ⟦{逆|さか}さ→逆さ：00358_sakasa⟧⟦{厳禁|げんきん}→厳禁：18021_genkin⟧ beside it, or print "↑ this side up" arrows, to avoid the confusion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {天地無用|てんちむよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧: a parcel marked "this side up"
- {取扱注意|とりあつかいちゅうい}・{天地無用|てんちむよう}: handle with care, this side up
